sections.content: The current tree is structurally healthy but still split between hard governance surfaces, prototype or pending control-plane artifacts, and a few very large orchestration seams. The earlier fail-open runtime issues are mostly closed in-tree now; the bigger remaining risks are seam concentration, raw governance JSON that is still not schema-backed, and a handful of empty or placeholder docs that are already wired into live code.

items: Convert the raw live mutation / code-scanning checklist and projection JSON blobs into schema-backed page artifacts, or move them out of the canonical docs tree if they are only intermediate evidence.
Keep decomposing AgentLoop into a thin orchestration shell; the next highest-value extraction targets are context/compiler.py, desktop/bridge_server.py, and conversation_runtime/runtime.py.
Treat dependency_surface_audit_v1 as a real cleanup slice: remove the unused direct dependencies or justify the remaining one.
Correct the documentation wording around public readiness so the audit artifacts and README tell the same conservative story.
Replace the empty/null surface report placeholder with a populated report or delete it if the lane is not ready to publish one.
Do not reopen the closed fail-open seams in ToolRuntime, DirtyGuard, checkpoint auth, or the subagent runtime path when patching adjacent modules.
